data.body:
AC3 RE-MEASURED at 8 of the consolidation children merged. It is trending FURTHER positive, not converging on negative, so the earlier n=3 reading was not an artefact of a small sample.

Per child (non-test files only, summed over each child's trailer commits on origin/main):
  6f18 StorePaths        add=211 del=125 net=+86
  1cf6 stamped lock      add=161 del=162 net=-1
  4329 cascade           add=148 del=73  net=+75
  111a replacement walk  add=96  del=97  net=-1
  7931 token twins       add=98  del=111 net=-13
  4cee fit_for_send      add=79  del=6   net=+73
  25b4 nested pytest     add=0   del=0   net=0    (its change is entirely under tests/)
  7e0d gate policy       add=25  del=3   net=+22
  SUBTOTAL add=818 del=577 NET=+241

Only three children are net-negative and none by more than 13 lines. Five children remain; for the total to reach negative they would have to average about -48 each, and nothing in their shape suggests that - they are extractions like the ones already measured, and every extraction so far has cost more in its documented owner module than it recovered from the call sites it emptied.

RECOMMENDATION, for a human decision rather than a unilateral edit: correct AC3 to measure what consolidation actually means - exactly one implementation per consolidated construct, which each child's construct-uniqueness guard already enforces and which AC1 already states - and keep the line count as a recorded observation rather than a pass/fail gate. The alternative readings are worse: forcing the number negative means deleting the 'why' docstrings that the plan-review and code-review gates both demand, trading a real quality signal for a proxy one; and closing the epic against a criterion it visibly failed would make the acceptance record dishonest.

SEPARATE FACTUAL DEFECT in this description: the Acceptance Criteria section says 'the fourteen named under Child responsibilities' for the consolidation class. There are now THIRTEEN - ticket 825c was unparented and closed out of scope earlier in this run. The nine hardening children named by alias are still accurate. A close review will flag the stale count, so it should be corrected whenever this description is next edited.
